key_insight: A correct final diagnosis can conceal unsafe intermediate decisions, and correcting an error can introduce new risks.
clinical_relevance: Clinical AI evaluation should assess the potential harm of tests, treatments and disposition decisions throughout care, not just diagnostic accuracy.
method: Replayed 300 cases checkpoint by checkpoint, revealing only evidence available at each step.
Scored each decision separately for potential harm and clinical validity, with LLM ratings calibrated against physician review.
Branched trajectories at the first actionable error to compare structured corrections with bare rejection.
evidence_signal: Among hospital trajectories reaching an acceptable diagnosis, 55.2% included moderate or severe potential harm; structured corrections resolved more first errors than bare rejection (73.6% vs 24.8%) but more often preceded new potentially unsafe decisions (30.2% vs 19.7%).
watch_item: These retrospective audits assess potential rather than observed patient harm, and physician calibration covered a stratified sample rather than every decision.
paper_title: Right Diagnosis, Unsafe Route: Auditing Clinical AI Decision Trajectories and Corrective Oversight for Validity and Potential Harm
